newsitem.title: USA: CBOT January soymeal contract settles at $241.50.
newsitem.headline: CBOT January soymeal contract settles at $241.50.

text.p: The Chicago Board of Trade January soymeal contract expired Wednesday at 1201 CST/1801 GMT but there was some confusion about closing trades and settlement prices.
The contract settled at $241.50 per ton, down $5.20 from Tuesday's close, according to CBOT's time and sales department.
CBOT price feeds initially posted a settlement price of $236.50 per ton about 30 minutes after contract expiry but a revised settlement of $241.50 was issued one hour later.
Price feeds indicated the last trade was at $248.00 per ton. That price was entered at 1157 CST, about three minutes before the contract expired.
But pit traders reported a final trade at $235.00 per ton, and a CBOT grain floor price supervisor said a $235.00 trade was entered at 12:02 CST.
CBOT price feeds indicated a closing range from $235.00 to $248.00 but there was no record of a trade at $235.00.
"Cargill sold about 10 lots and Continental two or three," one floor trader said. "They were long and got out but there wasn't anyone there to buy it, so it just caved in."
A spokeswoman for Cargill Inc declined comment and Continental Grain sources were not immediately available for comment.
Traders said the January/March spread on the modified close was offered at $3.00 per ton premium the January. But "there were no trades on the modified close," a trader said.
A CBOT spokesman said he was not aware of the price confusion but would look into it.
